words.intro: Germans go to court over things other people would discuss over a fence. A hedge, a barbecue, a cockerel: the local court hears them all, in black robes, with great care.

grammar[0].fact: German courts have strict rules on noise: no drilling on Sundays, quiet at night, and in some towns a limit on how long your dog may bark. There’s a *Rechtsschutzversicherung*, legal insurance, for this sort of thing, and many Germans have it.

grammar[1].fact: The highest court, the *Bundesverfassungsgericht*, sits in Karlsruhe, far from any government, on purpose. Germans trust it more than almost anything else, and any citizen may bring a complaint there. It’s very often the case that *Karlsruhe* has the last word on politics.

document.intro: A real page from a German handbook of about 1900, with model letters to a court, in Fraktur. Nothing has changed but the type. Find the section *Zurücknahme einer Klage*: a sausage maker has decided to drop his case.
document.fact: Books of model letters like this one, called *Briefsteller*, sold in huge numbers for a century. People who rarely wrote wanted the correct form for a court, a wedding or a marriage proposal. Now we have other tools for that.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Make each one an indirect question: Ich frage mich, …
document.tasks[1].items[0].answer: Ich frage mich, warum er die Klage zurückzieht.
reading.intro: Herr Müller is suing Herr Müller, his neighbour, over a cockerel. Frau Huber has come as a witness, in her best hat. The judge is reading out the statements made so far, and she would like to know whether any of it can be true.
reading.photos[0].caption: Karlsruhe: Hier hat das Recht das letzte Wort.
reading.fact: Neighbour disputes are so common that many states require mediation before you can sue, often by a *Schiedsmann*, a volunteer. The rulings are reported with pleasure: German courts have ruled on garden gnomes, and on cockerels too.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Report each sentence, in the past, with the Konjunktiv I.
reading.tasks[1].items[0].answer: Er sagte, der Hahn habe gekräht.
reading.tasks[1].items[2].answer: Er sagte, er habe keinen Hahn besessen.
